evals.name: ui-polish-landing-hero
evals.prompt:
polish this landing page hero — the headline feels generic and the CTA button has no visual weight. here's the JSX:

Transform your business with our solution
evals.expected_output: Applies impeccable sub-skill: diagnoses hierarchy/typography/contrast issues, proposes specific CSS or token changes (e.g., larger headline, primary button color, padding). Output is actionable, not 'make it pop'.

evals.name: anti-slop-readme-intro
evals.prompt: this README intro sounds like AI wrote it, can you fix it? 'In today's fast-paced development landscape, leveraging modern tools is paramount. Our solution seamlessly integrates a plethora of features that delve into the complexities of software engineering, delivering a truly remarkable experience.'
evals.expected_output: Applies stop-slop sub-skill: identifies 'in today's fast-paced', 'landscape', 'leverage', 'seamlessly', 'plethora', 'delve', 'truly remarkable'. Rewrites with varied sentence length, specific claims, no hedges, no fake enthusiasm. Preserves meaning (the product integrates features).

evals.name: code-polish-process-function
evals.prompt: tighten up this function without changing behavior: function process(data, flag, tmp) { if (flag == true) { for (var i = 0; i < data.length; i++) { if (data[i] != null) { data[i].processed = true; } } } }
evals.expected_output: Applies code-impeccable: renames 'data' -> 'items', 'flag' -> 'shouldProcess', removes 'tmp' (unused), replaces '== true' with truthy check, replaces 'var' with 'let'/'const', uses for-of or forEach, removes unnecessary null check if type proves non-null. Behavior preserved exactly.

evals.name: commit-message-mixed-changes
evals.prompt: write a commit message for these changes: I added JWT authentication to the user API, rejected expired tokens before decoding, and updated the docs to mention the new auth header
evals.expected_output: Applies commit-craft: identifies this should ideally be split into 3 commits (feat, fix, docs). For the combined commit, suggests 'feat(auth): add JWT authentication to user API' with a body explaining the implementation, the expired-token check, and the docs update. No AI tellss (no 'leverage', 'seamlessly', etc.). Imperative mood, <=50 char subject.

evals.name: code-review-react-pr
evals.prompt: review this PR — it adds a useUser hook that fetches user data on mount: function useUser(id) { const [user, setUser] = useState(null); useEffect(() => { fetch('/api/users/' + id).then(r => r.json()).then(setUser); }, []); return user; }
evals.expected_output: Applies code-review: identifies missing error handling (no try/catch, no .catch), missing loading state, missing cleanup (no abort controller), dependency array should include 'id' (current will only fetch once with initial id), no return of [user, loading, error] tuple. Loads skills/code-review/reference/react.md if needed for React-specific patterns. Provides prioritized feedback (P0 blocking / P1 should-fix / P2 nice-to-have).

evals.name: test-craft-vague-assertions
evals.prompt: is this test any good? test('user service', async () => { const result = await userService.create({ email: 'test@test.com' }); expect(result).toBeTruthy(); expect(result.id).toBeDefined(); expect(result.email).toBeTruthy(); });
evals.expected_output: Applies test-craft: identifies multiple issues — test name 'user service' doesn't describe behavior (should be 'createsUser_whenEmailIsValid' or similar), assertions are vague (toBeTruthy/toBeDefined instead of exact values), no edge case coverage (invalid email, duplicate email, missing fields), no assertion on side effects (was the user actually persisted?). Prescribes specific improvements without changing what the test currently asserts.

evals.name: craftsmanship-de-slop-dashboard
evals.prompt: my SaaS dashboard looks like every AI-generated app - dark background with purple gradient glows in the corners, three identical feature cards, emoji icons, and uppercase labels like OVERVIEW everywhere. fix it
evals.expected_output: Applies craftsmanship (design track): recognizes the banned-trope hits (gradient blobs, 3-card grid, emoji icons, screaming eyebrows). Prescribes one archetype (e.g., Quiet Luxury SaaS tokens), replacement layout (bento with hero tile), Lucide icon swap, sentence case. Runs the Design Read first, then the 7-axis gate before delivering. Commits to one visual world instead of restyling.

evals.name: craftsmanship-code-looks-ai
evals.prompt: reviewers keep saying my code looks AI-generated. here's a sample: // Helper function to process user data / async function processUserData(userId) { let result = null; try { const data = await fetchUser(userId); const isValid = await validateUserData(data); if (isValid == true) { result = await saveUserData(data); return true; } else { return false; } } catch (e) { console.error(e); return false; } }
evals.expected_output: Applies craftsmanship (code track): flags S6 (processUserData, data, result, isValid), S10 (if == true returning booleans, intermediate flags), S9 (catch-log-and-continue swallow), S1 (ghost 'helper function' comment), S14 (uniform defensive style). Prescribes domain-named function (activateAccount or similar per actual job), typed result instead of boolean soup, explicit error contract. Behavior-preservation rule stated; bug fixes flagged separately, not bundled.

evals.name: craftsmanship-landing-bespoke
evals.prompt: build a landing page for my freight-dispatch SaaS - but please don't make it look like the generic AI sites, I want it to feel like a real company built it
evals.expected_output: Applies craftsmanship (full stack of tracks): outputs a Design Read line first (freight dispatchers, chosen world, dials V/M/D). Picks a committed archetype (likely Technical Dense Terminal for the ops audience - not default purple SaaS). No gradient blobs, no 3-card grids, no eyebrow labels; tabular numerals; 8-state buttons; one authored motion moment; real dispatch-domain copy ('Track a load', not 'Transform your logistics'). Ends with the final assertion question before delivering.

evals.name: craftsmanship-design-sources-copy-and-suggest
evals.prompt: I'm building a marketing site with shadcn and I have no design direction. Can you find me some components I can actually copy - and maybe some sites to look at for inspiration?
evals.expected_output: Applies craftsmanship (design-sources reference): separates the two asks. Offers at most 2 code sources matched to the shadcn stack (e.g., Magic UI, Aceternity UI, or Animate UI) with license labels stated, and 2-3 look-only galleries matched to the no-direction signal (real-app polish vs avant-garde vs restraint) asking the user to pick what resonates. Stays under 5 links total. If it proceeds to copy a component, it states the discipline: license checked, mechanics lifted not identity, re-skinned to archetype tokens, provenance line in the commit.
